summary: Thomas A. Tweed works in religious and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Stanford University (~1979–1984), studying with William A. Clebsch, Lee Yearley, Peter N. Gregory, Gordon D. Kaufman, and doctoral supervisor William R. Hutchison, later serving as Professor of Religious Studies at UNC Chapel Hill (~1993–2008).
Thomas Athol Joyce was a scholar in history and archaeology. He studied at Hertford College (~1897–1901) and held a post at the British Museum (~1902–1938).

Thomas B. Ellis is a scholar of religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. He completed his PhD at the University of Pennsylvania and held a post as Assistant Professor of Religion at Appalachian State University (attested 2009).

Thomas Borchert is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who was a PhD candidate at the University of Chicago (attested 2005), studying under Bruce Lincoln and others. As of 2017, he was Associate Professor of Religion at the University of Vermont.

Thomas Burrow was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Christ's College, Cambridge, SOAS, and Annamalai University under E. J. Rapson and P. S. Subrahmanya Sastri. He served at the British Museum (1937–1944) and as Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford (1944–1976).
Thomas Christian Tychsen was a linguist and historian. After studying at Kiel University (~1777–1778) and the University of Göttingen (~1778–1781), he held a post at Göttingen from ~1785 to 1834.

Thomas Cleary worked in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and philosophy. He studied under E. Bruce Brooks, earned a PhD from Harvard University (~1970–1975), and obtained a JD from the University of California, Berkeley.

Thomas Doctor specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed doctoral research at the University of Lausanne under Tom Tillemans, an MA under Christian K. Wedemeyer, and studied at Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling under Chökyi Nyima Rinpoche and other teachers.

Thomas E. Crow studied at Pomona College and UCLA. He taught at institutions including CalArts, Chicago, Princeton, Michigan, Sussex, and Yale, served as director of the Getty Research Institute (2000–2007), and became Rosalie Solow Professor of Modern Art at NYU in 2007.

Thomas E. Wood works in philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his BA and PhD at the University of California, Berkeley (~1964–1974) and held posts at California State University, Fresno, and SUNY New Paltz.

Thomas Edward Colebrooke was an Indologist and historian who studied at Eton College, East India Company College, and under Jagannatha. He served as President (1864–1882) and Vice-President (until 1890) of the Royal Asiatic Society.

Thomas Freeman Yarnall works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Washington and Columbia University (PhD, 2003) under Robert A. F. Thurman, serving as Executive Editor at Columbia University (attested 2007).

Thomas Henry Huxley studied at Great Ealing School, Charing Cross Hospital Medical School (~1842–1845), Imperial College School of Medicine, and University College London. He held a post at Imperial College London from ~1854 to 1885.

Thomas James Mazanec specializes in Sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Calvin University, earned an MA from the University of Colorado, and completed doctoral work under supervisors Anna M. Shields, Stephen F. Teiser, and advisor Ping Wang.

Thomas Jülch is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Goethe University Frankfurt, the University of Hull (MA), the University of Heidelberg, and the University of Munich (PhD ~2006–2011), later working as a postdoctoral researcher at Ghent University (2013–2019).
Thomas Kintaert is an Indologist and scholar of Buddhist studies who held posts at the University of Vienna, attested in 2009 and 2022.
Thomas M. Hunter is a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He has served as Dean at the University of Virginia and held an affiliation at the University of British Columbia (attested 2011).

Thomas Nathan Patton is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Cornell University, where he studied under Anne M. Blackburn, and held a post at City University of Hong Kong (attested 2018).

Thomas Oberlies is an Indologist and linguist who studied under Albrecht Wezler and Paul Thieme. He held posts at the University of Tübingen (attested 1988), the University of Zurich (instructor, 1990), and the University of Freiburg (attested 2001).
Thomas P. Kasulis is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Japanology. He held a post at Ashland University (~1981–1991) and served as a professor at Ohio State University (~1991–2016).
